title: The shared signup code also grants unrestricted administrator access
impact: Anyone given the team access code to create an editor account can instead log in without an email and obtain access across projects and admin operations. Removing their account or resetting its password does not revoke this accountless session.
evidence: reproduce.mjs A01: POST /auth/login with the team code returned an admin JWT without sub. The normal signup path uses that same EDITOR_PASSWORD. This is a legacy compatibility path, but it defeats the current account roles.
fix: Disable accountless login in production; use separate, revocable invitations for signup. Require a real current account for every admin and project action. Rotate SESSION_SECRET after retiring legacy sessions.
verify: The signup code alone must never authenticate as admin; deleted or demoted accounts and old legacy cookies must fail authorization.

title: Staff can write into any known or invented upload staging ID
impact: The limited staff role can write files despite being barred from creating uploads. Any signed-in user knowing another staging ID can interfere with it. Staging IDs have no stored owner; unreferenced assets also lack ownership checks.
evidence: A02 used a staff account to PUT a chunk to ast_other_upload without creating an upload; HTTP 200 and the bytes were written. Init and chunk routes lack assetGuard/refuseStaff. Finalize is guarded but cannot undo the staging modification.
fix: Persist upload owner and state on creation; authorize init, chunk, finalize and cleanup against that owner. Refuse staff before reading upload bodies; reject unknown IDs. Give stored assets explicit ownership.
verify: Staff writes return 403; a second editor cannot initialize, resume, finalize or delete another editor's unused upload.

title: Unpublish then publish cannot restore a scene to live
impact: A routinely unpublished tour cannot be published again through the normal publish flow. The request fails while the scene remains offline.
evidence: A03: publish created @1, unpublish removed publishedVersion from the draft, and republish tried immutable @1 again and threw EEXIST. The same collision follows any published version because numbering restarts at 1.
fix: Keep a monotonic lastVersion counter independent of live status, or allocate from the highest historical version under a lock. Preserve immutable snapshots.
verify: Publish/unpublish/publish repeatedly; every attempt succeeds with a new increasing version, including after restoring older snapshots.

title: Version restore rolls back scene ownership
impact: Restoring history after a scene moves out of a shared project can transfer ownership to an earlier owner or null. The person restoring it can lose access, and the old owner may regain access.
evidence: A04 published as owner-a, detached the scene as owner-b, then restored version 1: ownerId changed back to owner-a. Restore protects propertyId but does not preserve current ownerId.
fix: Preserve ownership and all authorization metadata from the current draft during restore; restore only editable scene content.
verify: Restore a snapshot after transfer/detach/delete-project flows and assert current ownerId and permissions remain unchanged.

title: Booking read failures become empty inventory and can destroy records
impact: A corrupt reservation file or filesystem read error makes all inventory appear available. The next mutation can replace existing booking data with a new partial list, causing data loss and double bookings.
evidence: A05 wrote malformed JSON, readReservations returned [], then withReservations overwrote the damaged file with only a new record. The catch handles every error as an empty store.
fix: Treat only ENOENT as empty. Fail closed for invalid JSON, permission and disk failures; quarantine damaged files, alert operators, and restore from backup before accepting bookings.
verify: Malformed JSON and simulated read failures must return a controlled service error and leave the original file intact.

title: One-time reset links can be redeemed twice concurrently in file mode
impact: Two requests with the same reset link both succeed and race to choose the account password. File-backed role/password/reset updates can also overwrite each other because whole-file atomic writes do not serialize read-modify-write operations.
evidence: A06 called resetPassword twice through Promise.all with one token; both returned a user. The PostgreSQL implementation uses a conditional UPDATE and is stronger for this specific operation.
fix: Serialize all mutations per account, re-read and consume the token inside the lock; preferably use transactional database updates. Never allow a stale role write to revive old credentials.
verify: Concurrent redemption has exactly one success. Concurrent password reset and role change preserve both the new password and intended role.

title: Concurrent first signups both become administrators
impact: During first deployment, two people using the team code can both receive the initial administrator role. The first-account bootstrap is not serialized.
evidence: A07 created two users concurrently in an empty file store; both became admin. PostgreSQL has a similar check-then-insert condition; that database path was inspected, not executed.
fix: Bootstrap the first admin explicitly through an operator command, or protect initialization with a global transaction/advisory lock and an invariant.
verify: Concurrent initial registration creates at most one admin; staff invitation must never unexpectedly become admin.

title: Public enquiries accept nonexistent or unpublished scene references
impact: Invalid scene requests are saved and may trigger default-team email. This creates orphan leads and lets public callers submit against draft scene IDs. Valid published scenes moved between projects are routed using their current draft association.
evidence: A08 posted a valid guest form with not-a-real-space and received a persisted lead ID. Lookup uses getScene rather than getPublishedScene and does not reject an unresolved scene.
fix: Require a valid published scene or a valid public project entry point, derive project and scene labels from that public state, and reject unknown IDs before storage/email.
verify: Unknown/draft scenes cannot create leads; published tours route enquiries to the project shown to visitors.

title: Corrupt website state is silently treated as a new website
impact: A read failure returns null, so a subsequent draft save writes a new object and discards the prior publication, schedule and review state. The live site may disappear without a recoverable API error.
evidence: A09 wrote invalid JSON and readSite returned null. The draft route uses (await readSite(...)) ?? {} before overwriting the file.
fix: Only ENOENT means no site. Propagate corruption and disk errors; refuse mutations until recovery and retain backups.
verify: Invalid JSON yields a controlled error and a draft save cannot replace the damaged state.

title: External availability response size is checked after full buffering
impact: An engine endpoint can make the VPS allocate a large response despite the intended 64 KB limit. Public room-availability requests can invoke this path concurrently.
evidence: A10 supplied a mocked oversized response and proved text() completed before rejection. Code sets a timeout but does not cap streamed response bytes.
fix: Read a bounded stream, stop and cancel once the byte limit is reached; also enforce concurrency limits and a short timeout.
verify: A response over the cap is aborted before full consumption and peak memory stays bounded under simultaneous requests.

title: Suffix byte ranges return incorrect file content
impact: Media clients asking for bytes from the end receive the beginning instead, which can break MP4 metadata probing, seeking and other streaming clients.
evidence: A11: a 10-byte file containing 0123456789 returned 0123 for Range: bytes=-3. It should return 789 with Content-Range bytes 7-9/10.
fix: Implement suffix-length semantics and reject empty/invalid ranges; preferably use an established range parser.
verify: Verify bytes=-3, bytes=-100, bytes=3-, bytes=-0, zero-length files and large integer boundaries.

title: Byte ranges extending past EOF are rejected unnecessarily
impact: A valid request beginning inside a file but ending past EOF gets 416, creating avoidable media/download failures.
evidence: A12: Range bytes=0-99 against a 10-byte file returned 416. A satisfiable range should clamp the end and serve bytes 0-9.
fix: Clamp the end to bytes-1 when the start is valid; return 416 when no byte is satisfiable.
verify: Check bytes=0-99 returns the complete 10-byte file as 206, while bytes=10-99 returns 416.

title: Booking dates are validated by shape rather than calendar validity
impact: Impossible dates can enter event bookings. Some room dates normalize inconsistently or cause addDays/toISOString failures and 500 responses.
evidence: A13 eventProblem accepted 2026-11-31 with otherwise valid inputs. Regex YYYY-MM-DD alone cannot establish that the day exists.
fix: Use one strict calendar-date parser shared across server entry points; reject unless parsing and formatting round-trip exactly. Apply it to availability and staff marks too.
verify: Reject November 31, February 30, month 00/13 and day 00; accept valid leap days and enforce date windows.

title: One bad scene can break the entire studio scene list
impact: Listings parse every JSON file with Promise.all. A single malformed file fails the whole list; the account scan can similarly disrupt authentication for unrelated users.
evidence: A14 inserted one broken scene alongside a healthy scene and listScenes rejected with SyntaxError. Leads and file accounts have the same global parsing pattern, confirmed by inspection.
fix: Validate on write, isolate/quarantine individual damaged records during reads, report degraded health, and avoid exposing data outside the caller's scope while recovering.
verify: One bad record is detected and alerted without taking unrelated accounts, projects or public listings offline.

title: Website and hotspot bookings do not share room/hall inventory
impact: If a venue enables both booking channels for the same physical space, both can accept overlapping confirmed bookings. This is conditional on configuring both channels; embed-first operations can avoid the trigger.
evidence: A15 supplied a confirmed website hall booking; hallHotspotFree still returned true. Hall inventory filters different kinds. Website rooms and room hotspots likewise use separate identifiers and record kinds.
fix: Give each physical resource one inventory identifier across channels and centralize locking/availability. Until implemented, enforce one booking channel for a resource in configuration.
verify: Booking through either channel blocks overlapping requests/confirmations/marks through the other.

title: Multiple API processes bypass in-memory booking locks
impact: PM2 cluster mode, overlapping deploys or two API instances can both read the last available room/table and overwrite reservations. Rate limits multiply with each process and reset on restart. PostgreSQL accounts do not migrate booking storage.
evidence: Booking/stat queues and rate-limit counters are process-local Maps; all instances still write shared JSON files. No multi-process stress run was performed.
fix: Launch with exactly one API process until inventory uses database transactions/shared locks. Use shared rate limits when scaling; prevent old/new API overlap during deploy.
verify: Run a two-process last-table contention test after the storage fix; exactly one reservation succeeds and no records disappear.

title: Concurrent project/scene/site updates can lose edits and permission changes
impact: Atomic file replacement prevents torn JSON but not lost updates. Two editors can overwrite each other; a draft save can race a publish/scheduled publish, and two claims can both appear successful.
evidence: These operations read current objects, change them, and write with no shared per-record lock or revision check. publishDue explicitly shares the site file with draft and review operations.
fix: Add serialization and optimistic revision checks for every mutable entity, returning 409 on stale saves; use transactions for multi-file operations and ownership claims.
verify: Race publish/save, membership changes, claims and scheduled publish; all intended updates survive or receive explicit conflicts.

title: Uploads have no total quota, expiry or ZIP expansion budget
impact: An authorized account can fill VPS disk by sending many individually permitted chunks or a highly compressed ZIP. Abandoned staging data has no automatic retention policy. Disk exhaustion affects every tenant.
evidence: Only per-chunk limits are present. ZIP extraction writes entries without total uncompressed bytes/file-count/depth limits. No staging janitor was found. No destructive disk-fill experiment was run.
fix: Set per-upload and account quotas, extracted-byte/file/depth limits, free-space thresholds, and expired-upload cleanup. Enforce budgets while streaming, including during ZIP expansion.
verify: Small-budget tests stop oversized uploads safely, remove partial extraction, and leave capacity for normal bookings.

title: Concurrent chunks can overwrite each other after the offset check
impact: Duplicate/retried or overlapping requests can both see the same current offset and write to the same file. An offset-0 writer may truncate another writer's data.
evidence: The stat/offset check and createWriteStream are separate awaits with no per-file lock; the successful response reports the requested byte count rather than a protected committed state.
fix: Serialize chunk mutations per upload/file, atomically enforce expected offsets, and prevent finalize from running while writes are in progress.
verify: Two same-offset chunks produce one accepted write and one conflict; finalize cannot race an unfinished chunk.

title: Engine URL filtering does not prevent DNS-based private network access
impact: A studio author who configures an HTTPS hostname resolving to a private address can make the VPS contact internal services. This requires author control over availabilityUrl; it is not direct visitor URL input.
evidence: The filter checks the hostname string rather than resolved addresses. The source itself notes this gap. Redirects are correctly refused. No internal services were contacted in this review.
fix: Allowlist vetted engine hosts, or validate and pin all resolved IPv4/IPv6 addresses and enforce egress restrictions. Apply equivalent checks to every network hop.
verify: A controlled hostname resolving to loopback/private/link-local addresses is refused without initiating the connection.

title: Public room availability can trigger uncapped engine requests
impact: Changing date/guest combinations defeats the per-URL one-minute cache. Public traffic can create many simultaneous external requests and consume VPS and provider resources.
evidence: The room availability GET route has no rateLimiter check or shared concurrency cap; the booking submission route is separately rate limited. Bad engine responses are not cached.
fix: Rate limit availability reads, validate a bounded date/guest window, deduplicate in-flight engine calls, cap per-project concurrency and add failure caching/circuit breaking.
verify: A local fake engine sees bounded requests under a flood of varied dates; healthy callers still receive timely responses.

title: Attachment upload consumes its one-time key before saving the file
impact: If mkdir or file writing fails after reservation metadata commits, the upload key is gone and the reservation claims an attachment that cannot be downloaded. The guest cannot retry normally.
evidence: The reservation queue saves attachment metadata and deletes the key before filesystem writes begin. This ordering is visible in the route; disk failure was not injected.
fix: Stage the attachment first and commit metadata/key consumption only after durable storage succeeds, with rollback/cleanup and retry-safe operation IDs.
verify: Inject a storage failure: the guest can retry with the original key and the inbox does not show a nonexistent attachment.

title: The backup command does not back up PostgreSQL accounts or external local assets
impact: After switching accounts to PostgreSQL, restoring this archive does not restore users, password hashes or reset state. An ASSET_DIR outside DATA_DIR is also excluded in local-driver mode.
evidence: The backup script archives only DATA_DIR and optionally uploads that archive to S3. It never dumps PostgreSQL or separately archives ASSET_DIR. This is conditional on those deployment settings.
fix: Add tested PostgreSQL backups/PITR and a separate asset backup policy. Keep off-VPS copies, encrypt/restrict them, and document a complete restore including credentials/config held in an appropriate secret store.
verify: Restore into an empty machine/database; confirm accounts, permissions, booking history, attachments, scene JSON and every scan all work.

title: VPS deployment files are absent and production defaults are permissive
impact: There is no deploy directory despite references to it. Without explicit production environment and routing, the API enables development behavior, the browser calls localhost:4000, and the API binds all interfaces. Port conflicts silently move even in production.
evidence: No nginx/process-manager/deployment files exist in this checkout. NODE_ENV controls production secret checks, secure cookies, demo routes and localhost CORS. API_URL defaults to localhost; listen() has no host restriction and retries another port.
fix: Create reviewed nginx/TLS and process-manager configs; bind API to loopback or firewall it, pin ports and fail fast in production. Explicitly set NODE_ENV, strong secrets, CLIENT_ORIGIN, API URL and persistent data paths. Build frontend with production URLs.
verify: Test from an external machine: only intended HTTPS ports are open, cookies are secure, API routing works, restarts retain data, and a port conflict fails visibly.

title: Some Express 4 async authentication handlers do not forward rejected promises
impact: A database or account-file failure during these handlers can become an unhandled rejection instead of reaching the JSON error handler. On Node's default handling this can terminate the API process.
evidence: The server uses Express 4. requireAdmin and GET /session are bare async functions without try/catch or a promise wrapper, unlike most other routes. A real database-outage/process-crash test was not run.
fix: Wrap every async route/middleware in a rejection-forwarding helper or consistently catch and next(err). Test failures at all authentication lookup points.
verify: Force account lookup to reject and assert a sanitized 5xx response, no hung request, and continued API health.

title: Server lockfile includes a qs version flagged by npm audit
impact: The installed server dependency tree has one moderate advisory. This is not proof that the vulnerable qs.stringify comma option is reachable in this application.
evidence: npm audit --prefix server --json reported GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw (qs.stringify comma-format TypeError DoS), affected range 6.7.0 through 6.16.0, fix available. Frontend audit reported zero known advisories at audit time.
fix: Update the affected transitive dependency through a compatible parent/lockfile update, review changes, rerun audit and application checks. Avoid blind forced major upgrades.
verify: Server audit has no remaining advisory and query parsing/API regressions still pass. Source: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw

title: Private booking attachments are missing from git ignore rules
impact: New guest PDF/Word attachments under the default data directory can be accidentally added to source control, unlike users, leads and reservations which are ignored.
evidence: Attachments are written to DATA_DIR/attachments/<project>; .gitignore has no server/src/data/attachments/ rule. No attachment contents or credentials were copied into this report.
fix: Ignore the default attachments directory and prefer runtime DATA_DIR outside the source checkout. Inspect staged changes for private data before commits.
verify: git check-ignore confirms a sample default-path attachment is ignored; no guest files are tracked.

title: Tour defaults assume Nepal even when the venue uses another timezone
impact: The old visitor-local-clock issue is fixed for Nepal venues, but the hotspot form calls venueDay without the project's configured timezone. A venue elsewhere can still receive dates inconsistent with server rules.
evidence: Source inspection: form defaults and min dates use venueDay() with the Nepal default; backend uses the published booking.timezone. Not reproduced in a browser.
fix: Expose the venue clock/timezone to the hotspot form and pass it to every date default/min helper; prefer server-returned today for public booking rules.
verify: Check venues in Kathmandu, Honolulu and Auckland around midnight with visitors in different timezones.

title: Tour first render waits for every published scene in the project
impact: A large project requires all scene documents before mounting 3D. The shared API client has no timeout, so a stalled related scene request can keep the visitor on Opening the tour indefinitely.
evidence: TourClient fetches all matching project scenes with Promise.all before setGate ready. This is a scaling/reliability risk, not a measured first-frame regression.
fix: Load the requested starting scene first, hydrate the rest lazily, and add bounded timeouts/cancellation and useful retry states. Preserve access checks.
verify: With one sibling scene delayed or failed, the requested healthy scene still opens within the first-frame target on a real mobile device.

title: Public marketing content still contains editorial placeholders
impact: Visitors can encounter unfinished copy and unresolved service/policy facts. This lowers trust and means the public policy text may not describe the final deployment.
evidence: Source includes visible TBI/TBC markers for formats, licensing, address and providers. Draft policy handling is intentional, but the final content still needs owner review.
fix: Replace placeholders with verified business facts and deployment-specific policy text; hide unfinished sections until approved. Do not invent business or policy claims.
verify: Crawl rendered public pages for TBI/TBC, broken contact actions and draft content before launch.
